title: Cell-free DNA Biospecimen Collection and Processing
author: NCI Biorepositories and Biospecimen Research Branch

steps.title: Prepare Collection Tubes
steps.instruction: Select and label collection tubes with unique, unambiguous identifiers using labels robust to frozen storage, water, and solvents.

substeps.instruction: Use EDTA tubes (optimally K2 EDTA) or acid citrate dextrose to prevent coagulation; avoid heparin and citrate.
Use Streck Blood Collection Tubes (BCT) or other cfDNA stabilizing tubes if processing delays > 2 h are anticipated.
Collect 1-2 10 mL tubes (acceptable range 2.7-10 mL) depending on downstream application.
If using K2 EDTA tubes, pre-chill on ice for at least 5 minutes prior to collection.
If using cfDNA stabilizing tubes, maintain tubes at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Patient for Venipuncture
steps.instruction: Ensure the patient is properly positioned and prepared for blood draw.

substeps.instruction: Patient must be seated for at least 5 minutes before venipuncture.
Position arm on a slanting armrest to create a straight line from shoulder to wrist.

steps.title: Perform Venipuncture
steps.instruction: Extract blood from the patient following aseptic technique and specific needle guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Apply a tourniquet 3-4 inches above the venipuncture site with enough pressure for vein visibility; have patient form a fist.
Select median, cubital, basilic, or cephalic veins; avoid collection from a port.
Clean site with an antiseptic wipe in a circular motion starting at the insertion site.
Once dry, anchor the vein by placing thumb 2 inches below the site and pulling skin taut.
Insert a 21-23 gauge butterfly needle with Luer adapter (or a vacutainer needle) at a 30° angle.
Push the evacuated tube into the hub/adapter, ensuring additives do not touch the stopper or needle end.
Once blood flow is established, release the tourniquet (total time < 1 min) and ask patient to open hand.
Optimally, discard the first 0.5-3 mL of blood before collecting EDTA plasma.

steps.title: Post-Collection Handling
steps.instruction: Complete the blood draw and stabilize the samples.

substeps.instruction: Remove the tube after filling, leaving the needle inserted until all tubes are filled.
Place gauze over the puncture site and remove the needle.
Slowly and gently invert each tube 8-10 times.
Minimize agitation of blood after initial inversion during any processing delay.

steps.title: Store Blood Tubes
steps.instruction: Store tubes vertically based on the tube type used.

substeps.instruction: K2 EDTA tubes: Store vertically on ice.
Streck BCT or cfDNA stabilizing tubes: Store vertically at room temperature.

steps.title: Primary Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge blood to separate cells from plasma.

substeps.instruction: For EDTA blood: Centrifuge optimally within 2 hours of venipuncture (acceptable: up to 4 h at room temperature or 24 h at 4°C).
For Streck BCT: Room temperature or ambient storage/transport for up to 3 days is acceptable.
Centrifuge at 800-1600 g for 20 min at 4°C or room temperature.

steps.title: Plasma Recovery and Secondary Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Isolate plasma and remove remaining cell debris.

substeps.instruction: Transfer plasma to a new Lo-Bind (or equivalent) container, carefully leaving the buffy coat behind.
Perform a second centrifugation at 14000-16000 g for 10-20 min at room temperature or 4°C (filtration is an acceptable alternative).

steps.title: Aliquot and Store Plasma
steps.instruction: Divide plasma into storage tubes suitable for -80°C.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot volumes ranging from 400 µL to > 10 mL depending on extraction method.
Store plasma post-centrifugation: optimally ≤ 3 h at 4°C, up to 3 months at -20°C, or 9 months at -80°C (long-term -80°C is generally acceptable).
For NIPT: Refrigerated storage of Streck plasma for 3-4 days is acceptable.

steps.title: Extract and Quantify cfDNA
steps.instruction: Extract cfDNA from plasma and determine concentration.

substeps.instruction: Thaw frozen plasma at room temperature and extract cfDNA immediately after the first thaw.
Use a circulating nucleic acid kit or equivalent kit for extraction.
Quantify cfDNA using real-time or digital PCR with multiple amplicons (fluorometry is also acceptable).
Evaluate cfDNA suitability for subsequent analysis via real-time PCR.

steps.title: Store and Validate cfDNA
steps.instruction: Store extracted DNA and validate the analytical assay.

substeps.instruction: Store extracted cfDNA as aliquots at -20°C; use only after the first thaw.
Validate each analytical assay for accuracy, precision, specificity, and sensitivity using suitable reference material.
